name: Matthias Hallett

bio.statement: Hallett's voters' pamphlet statement lists his occupation as estate planning attorney.
Hallett's pamphlet statement lists a JD from Vermont Law School and a BS from Columbus State University.

bio.statement: Hallett's pamphlet statement lists prior service as deputy probate clerk at the Muscogee County Probate Court.
bio.excerpt: Deputy Probate Clerk, Muscogee County Probate Court

positions.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Hallett says police should be present, visible and known in the neighborhoods they serve.
positions.excerpt: Police should be present, visible, and known in the neighborhoods they serve

positions.statement: Hallett's pamphlet statement says Portland cannot tax its way out of a shrinking base and must grow it back.

positions.statement: Hallett's pamphlet statement says he will set strict permitting timelines with automatic escalation when projects stall.

positions.statement: Hallett's pamphlet statement calls for right-sizing the business tax structure to keep Portland competitive.

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 21 District 3 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF (with the full and large-print county pamphlets tried where the statement PDF was a scan; the pamphlet's candidate index marks candidates who filed no statement) plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form linked from portland.gov's 2026 city candidates page; (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the three articles that cover the whole District 3 field: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 3 council race' (2026-10-07), Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 3' (2026-09-09) and Portland Tribune 'Meet the Portland City Council District 3 candidates' (2026-10-13; Q&A — the Tribune says Sollitt, Pham, Parker, McCormick, Kelly and Frankenstein did not respond and Tucker withdrew). Multi-winner race: OPB states three council seats are available in District 3. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Discrepancy: the Portland Mercury says Hallett received his bachelor's degree from the University of Georgia, while his pamphlet statement lists a BS from Columbus State University and his filing form lists UGA as attended through junior year; the Mercury bio line was not used. Filing form URL slug misspells 'mattias'.
